llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究SLM制备Ti-6Al-4V的马氏体形成与控制，属于工艺参数优化，但与生物医用植入物的多孔结构、应力屏蔽或疲劳性能无关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper focuses on microstructure evolution in SLM Ti-6Al-4V without addressing porous structure, stress shielding, fatigue, or osseointegration relevant to biomedical implants.

summary_zh.motivation: 探索SLM工艺参数对Ti-6Al-4V马氏体形成的影响
summary_zh.method: 改变激光功率和扫描速度进行SLM实验，通过XRD和SEM表征
summary_zh.result: 高冷却速率促进α'马氏体形成，低速率生成α+β片层组织
summary_zh.validation: 实验表征对比不同工艺参数下的微观组织

summary_en.motivation: To understand how selective laser melting process parameters control martensite formation in Ti-6Al-4V alloys.
summary_en.method: Ti-6Al-4V samples were fabricated by SLM under varying laser power and scanning speed, followed by XRD and SEM analysis.
summary_en.result: High cooling rates favor α' martensite while lower rates produce α+β lamellar structures.
summary_en.validation: Microstructural characterization validated the effect of process parameters on phase composition.

papers.title: Fabrication of heat sinks by Selective Laser Melting for convective heat transfer applications
papers.abstract: In this paper, the forced convective heat transfer performance of heat sinks produced by Selective Laser Melting (SLM) was experimentally investigated. Three heat sinks comprising pin fins of circular, rectangular-rounded and aerofoil geometries were fabricated by SLM from aluminium alloy AlSi10Mg powder. The heat sinks were tested in a rectangular air flow channel for convective heat transfer performance. Experiments performed for Reynolds numbers ranging from 3400 to 24,000 show that the heat transfer performances of the aerofoil and rectangular-rounded heat sinks exceeded those of the circular heat sink. Using the cylindrical heat sink as a benchmark, the average enhancements in the normalised Nusselt numbers were computed to be 15.0% and 21.4% for the rectangular-rounded and aerofoil heat sinks, respectively. It was demonstrated that SLM can be employed to design and fabricate heat sinks of customised geometries for heat sink applications.

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the feasibility of using Selective Laser Melting to fabricate heat sinks with customized geometries for enhanced convective heat transfer.
summary_en.method: Three aluminium alloy heat sinks with circular, rectangular-rounded, and aerofoil pin fins were manufactured via SLM and experimentally tested in a rectangular air flow channel.
summary_en.result: The aerofoil and rectangular-rounded pin fin designs showed average Nusselt number enhancements of 21.4% and 15.0% respectively compared to the circular design.
summary_en.validation: Experimental measurements over a range of Reynolds numbers from 3400 to 24000 provided validation of the heat transfer performance.

papers.title: System development, formability quality and microstructure evolution of selective laser-melted magnesium
papers.abstract: A selective laser melting (SLM) system, which consisted of a fibre laser, a three-dimensional motion platform and a motion control system, was developed in this study. The effect of process parameters on the microstructure evolution of SLMed magnesium parts was investigated. The results revealed that under an irradiation of laser energy density <3.0 J/mm, the powder remained in the discrete state. At a laser energy density 3.0–6.0 J/mm, the powder partially melted and sintered together, yielding incompact tracks. As the energy density increased to 6.0–12.0 J/mm, the powder fully melted forming continuous and smooth tracks. With a further increase in the laser energy density evaporation of the powder occurred. Dense magnesium parts free of pores and cracks were successfully fabricated with the optimal energy density of 10.0 J/mm. The immersion experiment revealed that the degradation product was mainly consisted of Mg(OH)2, which slowed down the degradation rate acting as a protective layer.

summary_en.motivation: To develop an SLM system for magnesium and investigate the effect of process parameters on microstructure evolution.

papers.title: Design considerations for patient-specific surgical templates for total hip arthroplasty with respect to acetabular cartilage
papers.abstract: Patient-specific instruments (PSIs) are clinically used to support the surgeon during a planned intervention. The planning is typically done based on volumetric image data from medical imaging systems, e.g. computed tomography (CT). The PSI uses the known surface structure of a bone for orientation during the intervention. Some surfaces of human bone are covered with a layer of cartilage which is hardly visible in clinically applied CT-imaging. This experimental study investigates ten different PSI designs and their effect to the overall accuracy when neglecting the cartilage in the design process. Therefore, a model of an acetabulum is used to simulate the use case of PSI in total hip arthroplasty. The concept of the different designs is to create structural elasticities in the PSI to avoid shifting of the whole instrument and rather have a small part of it deformed by cartilage. A needle array structure, for instance, should also be able to oust or penetrate remaining soft tissue in the acetabulum.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文关注髋臼软骨的个性化手术导板设计，未涉及股骨柄假体的应力屏蔽或微动分析。
llm.why_not_core: This paper focuses on acetabular cartilage and surgical template design, not on femoral stem stress shielding, micromotion, or proximal femur biomechanics.

summary_zh.motivation: 探讨髋臼软骨对个性化手术导板精度的影响
summary_zh.method: 设计十种不同结构的导板并实验测试其变形与移位
summary_zh.result: 发现针阵列结构能有效适应软骨层并减少导板移位
summary_zh.validation: 利用髋臼模型进行实验验证

summary_en.motivation: To investigate how neglecting acetabular cartilage in patient-specific instrument design affects surgical accuracy.
summary_en.method: Ten different PSI designs with structural elasticities were tested on an acetabulum model to assess deformation and displacement.
summary_en.result: A needle array structure effectively accommodated cartilage thickness and minimized instrument shifting.
summary_en.validation: Experimental validation using an acetabular model simulating total hip arthroplasty.
